text_raw: I’m glad I can use notion on iPad, but man… I use this for simple writing, google docs level stuff, and this app has a lot off issues. I’m using the official iPad keyboard, and it’s absolutely awful with clicking. It’s hard to explain, but I feel I have to stop moving and click HARD every time I want to to start typing. And now since the new update, it just straight up doesn’t work. I click, the type line appears, then it unselects itself. I have to click several times, eventually it works. That’s awful. Fix that please. Another issue, the little taskbar is awful on iPad, I can’t move it around or out of the way with a swipe, I have no idea how to change the colour of text effectively since when I open that menu it’s hell to go back. There’s more, and after using this app for a year I can probably raise a lot more issues and I reckon they’d be fixed - Notion seems like a great company and they’ve made a fantastic product. But it almost seems like these issues have gone unnoticed? Perhaps low on priority? … if you can sort these sooner rather than later, that’d be very appreciated. Thanks for your time.

text_raw:
Doesn’t work. At all. I know this app has almost 70k mostly good reviews but I simply cannot get it to do the most basic of what it is meant to do, which is build a database. 

I’m not tech incompetent at all, even though I started questioning that fact after so much frustration when getting started. Am I just missing something?!

The backslash does. Not. Work. I tried on the app. I tried in the browser. I made sure the / is not a \ and that I’m not entering it in a forbidden field or table. I watched all the videos. They all start with “type /database” 

I did. Which resulted in a “/database” appearing when I type and that’s it!!! No menu! No options!! I tried Reddit. I tried YouTube. I tried the official Notion tutorial. text_raw:
العراق. اعطيت التطبيق نجمة واحدة لكوني لم استطع استخدامه او تجربته! بسبب مشكلة اتجاه النص العربي (RTL) و بسبب عدم توفّر واجهة عربية (Arabic UI)، و في ادناه تحليل المشكلة و الحل الذي ينبغي على المطورين اعتماده.

- وصف المشكلة (Issue Description):
    
    يعاني المستخدمون العرب من قلب اتجاه السطر وتخبّط المحاذاة أثناء الكتابة بالعربية داخل نَوشَن (Notion). يظهر الخلل خصوصًا عند إدراج كلمات إنجليزية قصيرة داخل سطر عربي، مما يؤدي إلى اضطراب اتجاه النص وعدم اتساق العرض.
    
- خطوات إعادة الإنتاج (Steps to Reproduce):
    1. اكتب سطرًا عربيًا يبدأ بحرف عربي.
    2. أضف مصطلحًا إنجليزيًا بين قوسين بعد كلمة عربية مثل: اسمي احمد (ahmed) وأسكن بغداد (Baghdad).
    3. لاحظ تغيّر اتجاه السطر أو اختلاط المحاذاة يمينًا ويسارًا، خاصة عند نسخ السطر أو تعديله.
- النتيجة الحالية (Actual Result):
    
    اختلال اتجاه السطر وتخبّط المحاذاة، مما يصعّب القراءة والكتابة ويشوّه التنسيق.
    
- النتيجة المتوقعة (Expected Result):
    
    ثبات اتجاه النص العربي من اليمين إلى اليسار (RTL) حتى مع وجود مصطلحات إنجليزية قصيرة ضمن السطر، مع محاذاة مستقرة وموثوقة.
    
- الأثر (Impact):
    
    تجربة الكتابة للمستخدم العربي تتأثر سلبًا، ويصعب استخدام نَوشَن (Notion) لإدارة المحتوى اليومي أو الاحترافي. هذا يسبب إحباطًا ويجبر البعض على التوقف عن استخدام التطبيق.
    
- البيئة (Environment):
    
    لغة الكتابة العربية (Arabic). المشكلة تظهر في الويب (Web) وتطبيق الهاتف (Mobile App) على حد سواء بحسب ملاحظات المستخدمين.
    
- أمثلة سطرية (Examples):
    - اسمي احمد (ahmed) وأسكن بغداد (Baghdad)
    - سكربت الحلقة (Script) والعناصر الأساسية (Key Points)
- طلب التحسين (Request):
    1. دعم كامل لاتجاه النص العربي من اليمين إلى اليسار (RTL) داخل المحرّر.
    2. إضافة خيار لغة عربية للواجهة (Arabic UI) ضمن الإعدادات (Settings).
    3. تحسين التعامل مع المصطلحات الإنجليزية القصيرة داخل السطور العربية دون إفساد الاتجاه.
- ملاحظات إضافية (Additional Notes):
    
    يفضّل توفير إعداد لإجبار اتجاه الفقرة عربيًا عند الحاجة، وخيار تنسيق سريع يضمن عدم قلب الاتجاه حتى مع الرموز والروابط.

text_raw:
great for organisation but paywalls & ai are annoying. As a high school student who struggles with time management and organisation, I can say Notion is great for helping me stay on track, remember everything I need to do, and the layout of pages within pages, databases, embeds, toggles, etc are really useful for organisation. I also like to use notion for personal organisation outside of school with my friends, so being able to collaborate is nice. However the collaboration process is a little complicated and annoying sometimes.

However, paywalls make the experience restrictive, and I understand the need for funding everything from the business point of view but what’s annoying is once I run out of “blocks”, deleting them and even emptying out my trash doesn’t change it so I could delete everything and still not be able to do anything else with my workspace, forcing me to make yet another account.

AI is also just straight up so horrible for the environment because of the amount of water and electricity it uses, and it promotes anti-intellectualism because users become dependent on it for writing, thinking, and making decisions, to the point it’s affecting education all over the world. It also promotes anti-social behaviour and has been used in harmful (and on occasion illegal) ways.

I hope you as a company take my experience into account as a user of four years to improve your app.

text_raw:
Fix Some Features. I got recommended Notion for documents and images. The good thing about Notion is that when viewing images, you can zoom in perfectly and the image is not compressed in any way. I used this feature for a good while, and I always found it useful.

But, recently, after the new updates, the process has gotten a little bit tedious when captioning images, as the three dots are no longer there at the top-right corner of the image so you can easily select the "Caption" option instead of holding on the image to do so. I really preferred the three-dots option. 

Also, when captioning an image, it causes the app to bug out, not allowing you scroll while editing the caption. This bug has frustrated me so much.

And lastly, when wanting to view an image directly, you used to be able to just tap on the image to view it. But, now you have to hold the image and press "View Original." That's just too cumbersome and tedious to keep doing over and over again. I want to be able to view images right away.

To summarize:
- The three-dots at the top right of each image was always very useful to quickly use other options such as captioning, but now its gone. I want it back.

Great, and still… There’s a lot of things I like about Notion. I’ve used it for years now, and really see its benefits. And, it needs work. The AI integrations can be obnoxious, like when you’re trying to upload photos and you accidentally hit the new button they’ve added for AI notes. It takes forever to figure out how to get it off the screen. 

Uploading photos in general is sometimes a liability. If something happens to the connection, photos you think are almost uploaded stop midway and can’t be recovered—so if you’re taking photos directly into Notion which is how we want to use it, it may not save them. 

If you do upload them and need to download them, something recently changed where it takes extra steps to just get to the photo to do so. I guess my primarily complaint is not being able to trust Notion with managing my photos—which is crucial for our business and how we use Notion.

Breadcrumbs are a core part of UX and aid in accessibility. 

They tell us where we are.

Add them back to the top of the page so users don’t have to click an extra two buttons just to see the breadcrumb list.

text_raw:
Loads of potential, partly realized. I’ve only used Notion for about a year (coming from Coda) but I’ve enjoyed the ease of use and aesthetic. The mobile app is a bit clunky and missing some functionality. For instance, there doesn’t appear to be a way to edit a links properties in the mobile version. If you click on the property, it takes you to the linked site. If you press and hold, you have the option of opening the link, copying the link, or sharing the link. No way to delete or edit. And the inability to move to a new line within a text property is killing the functionality of this app as a note taking tool for me. You cannot move columns or adjust property positions in the app. Just three examples of simple functionality that seems to have been overlooked by Notion. 
The app gets very unstable sometimes, especially the filters. Almost every time I use an advanced filter, the app freezes and I have to force reset.

They filter all their support requests through an AI bot and if you try to get a human, you can't. I didn't sign up to pay for that. I paid to be able to get a human when I run into issues. So I've cancelled my subscription. They've gone too far and destroyed what used to be a great product.

text_raw:
Ultimate flexibility. Some elbow grease requires. Notion in a word - flexible. 

Simplicity. Probably not. 

That’s not a criticism. That’s testament to how much you can do with it. 

A file manager is simple. Make some folders, store some files. Search them. Useful? Yes. Powerful? Not really. Flexible. No. 

It’s got a singular purpose. 

Notion is flexible and powerful. The trade off is knowing where to start. 

Notion can be a workflow tool. It can be a blog hosting platform. It can manage projects. Organise data for you and tag it. Be a research vault, holding articles, audio, imagery and video, all tailored and presented just the way you like it. Not a flat structure of files. No, think a rich webpage with links passing to other pages, embedded media. The works. 

And it’s not that hard to get any of it working. Notion does a lot to make this as easy as it can be. It’s all GUI driven. It’s impressive. 

Sure it has quirks. Could you get something this flexible to work without them? Probably not. 

You will struggle to find a product as feature rich. Its AI tooling isn’t just a gimmick either. It can truely help you manage and create content. 

Ask yourself - do you need this much in a tool? If you need a fantastic collaboration platform; a place to collect and organise your research project; a project management tool to help run your SMB; a way to effectively manage you local soccer club - notion could be your answer. 

If you just want somewhere to save your photos, or store some files, it’s overkill. 

Overall an excellent product in the right context.

Great tool but no dynamic text sizes for accessibility? I use this tool both personally and professionally. I also use it on both Android and iOS. It works great and is my go to for internal docs, notes, kanban boards. You name it - other than spreadsheets! Great tool!

I am frustrated that the iOS version doesn’t seem to support dynamic text sizes for page content. I need the default text size larger and, while the menus, titles, and buttons seem to get the larger dynamic text size, the page content remains the same size - somewhat invalidating the setting. It seems odd that this doesn’t work properly on iOS given that this isn’t even an issue on Android. This has been a problem for a while now and I would appreciate attention to this matter - a fix, and workaround (that actually works - accessibility settings per app and increasing it there also doesn’t work).

Rigid and unhelpful. If you have been on the internet in the last decade or so, this is a HUGE step back. It is rigid, with nonsensical rules that they refuse to change. There are a host of things you can't change that aren't just unhelpful, but maddening. Don't want comments on your page? Too bad. They don't care. Don't want a list of every connection your page has BEFORE you get to the actual page information? Nope. You can't. They know it's a problem and don't care. Want to simply move that issue to the bottom? Oh no. That would be crazy. 

This might be a decent product if they had half the options and functionality they claim to have. I'm a few hours in and feeling like I'm back the the internet circa 1998. Do better.

text_raw:
Another Poor iPad Version. It’s wild to me that the iPad version of this app is as poorly optimised as it is. After getting a nice big iPad to handle simple notes, journals, and other organisation, I sort of assumed Notion would’ve figured out a satisfying experience to mirror all the other instances. Maybe I had my expectations out of whack. It’d be one thing if it was just the iPhone app (still disappointing) but certain functions just straight up don’t work, and major ones no less, like simply moving sections around.

I want to love Notion, but it’s so disappointing to know that something so well suited to the purpose of Notion as the iPad (at least, in my opinion) clearly isn’t a priority.

But hey, at least their shareholders got another AI chat bot to peddle in meetings.

I was really excited to use this app and I enjoyed using it to the point that I decided to buy the business Level subscription from them at $21 a month according to their website. When I tried to start the subscription, their Web app rerouted me to the iPhone App Store, and proceeded with the charging for the subscription. It wasn’t until further inspection that I realized they rerouted me out of the business plan into a plus subscription and nearly double the website price for the same service. The service I needed had necessary integrations like GitHub, Google applications, etc. Instead, I just received a slightly expanded, Nerfed version of the free subscription and didn’t get any of the features that I needed by actually paying for it, which were only three dollars more off their website. They don’t even offer that subscription through the App Store so they’re rerouting people and hoping they don’t notice that they’re being charged for the tier less a double the website price and three dollars less than the pro model which has like 50 more features than what there giving you. text_raw:
Lots of fixes needed instead of new features. I use this app a lot, and it is wonderful. For 2 years, I’ve waited and tried to use iOS shortcuts to upload photos to database directly or just create a new page with a template included. For some reason they’ve done the most random work on iOS shortcuts. New automations are created, but there’s still no way to create a new page with the default template. 

It even says “template” as a parameter in shortcuts, but they haven’t implemented it in the shortcut.  There’s also no way to create new page in shortcuts with certain blocks.

Other smaller problems: The buttons inside Notion are convenient but missing tons of options to make it usable consistently. Links colors should be able to be changed from the default color, i.e I always want blue links instead slightly off gray. 

Also, the AI option should have an option to always yes disable it. It’s useless to me, and I will never use. It just gets in the way, and I’ve definitely accidentally clicked it. I know it’s to make money, but please let me have a hidden setting to never see it again.

text_raw:
Mostly useless. Put me in the category of "Huh?!". It's a tool to organize notes and task lists - so what?  There's no prioritization, little to no structure at the list/item level, reminder options are fixed and mostly useless.

text_raw:
Good platform, terrible app. I’ve been a Notion power user since about 2018. I rely on it for hours every day. The overall trajectory of the platform has been great since then, but the mobile app has always had issues. And it seems they are getting worse. Just about every app update these days introduces major workflow breaking bugs. For example, it worked perfectly yesterday until I updated to the latest version today, and now mobile dictation is completely broken. 

Currently, with many multi select properties, sometimes opening the selection window completely crashes the app and it must be manually restarted.

Each update is like Russian Roulette: perhaps you’ll gain some small feature, and hopefully you won’t also get a new bug that completely interferes with usability. A bit hyperbolic? Sure. My business runs on this platform and bugs that break basic usability cost me. 

Will update this review if they manage to roll out 3 consecutive updates without breaking anything major.

text_raw: Powerful, flexible, and great for staying organized. Notion is one of the most versatile productivity apps I’ve used. It works well whether you’re managing personal notes, tracking projects, or collaborating with a team. The flexibility is its biggest strength—you can start simple and gradually build more complex systems as your needs grow. I especially like how everything lives in one place: documents, databases, tasks, and ideas are easy to connect and reorganize. The interface is clean and modern, and once you get used to it, workflows feel very natural. Syncing across devices is reliable, which makes it easy to switch between phone, tablet, and desktop without losing context. There is a learning curve at the beginning, but plenty of templates and community resources help you get started quickly. Overall, Notion is a powerful tool for anyone who wants more control over how they organize information and work. It’s not just a note-taking app—it’s a flexible workspace that adapts to how you think and work.

I do recognize that the iPhone SE has a smaller screen than most phones, and it’s possible that this is a dynamic layout issue that only happens on smaller screens. Even if that’s the case, losing the button for an AI prompt area that I can’t even use feels really bad.

The rest of the app and Notion features are working wonderfully.

text_raw:
Intentional Lack of Important, Basic Features. Probably the worst notes app I’ve ever had the pleasure of experiencing, all because they’ve done the work to be found near top search results through sponsored means, whether that be comments or ratings. 

It makes no sense why another individual would have to create an account just to see my document, especially if they’re already going to be defaulted to read-only mode. This ultimately makes this app incredibly difficult to work with when working with others, as the question, “Why didn’t I just make it in a text document with word or Google Docs?” There are plenty of open-source options. 

Don’t even get me TOO started on the fact that the app allows offline downloads, but clearly is so insecure in its desire to consume user data and user interactions that you, as the user, are not allowed to even OPEN THE APP when you’ve disabled “Use Cellular Data” in your phone’s settings. 

Actually pointless. I’ll unfortunately be moving all of my notes over to a smarter, more competitive app; wherein I don’t have to pay $20+ a month for automatic offline downloads, just to not be able to use the app if I turn cellular data off. Actually insane. Unlucky.

If you’re a small biz owner and don’t want to spend on software you can literally make pages shareable and have a website, run emails, have a calendar etc.

Love it overall, but a few issues on iPad mini. :)
I really love the integrated AI. It’s incredibly helpful and makes my workflow so much smoother. Thank you for adding this feature.

:(

It would also be much more convenient if all private notes could be listed without needing to tap “More”. After tapping it, the list does not scroll properly anyway, which makes navigation frustrating.

Thank you for your work on the app. I’m looking forward to future improvements.

text_raw:
Best notetaker. Notion has become one of my favorite tools for taking notes and organizing ideas. I like how flexible it is. You can turn a simple page into a full workspace with lists, databases, and structured notes without it feeling complicated. Everything stays in one place, which makes it easy to keep track of projects, thoughts, and daily planning.

What I appreciate the most is how customizable it is. I can structure my notes exactly how I want instead of forcing them into a rigid template. It works just as well for quick brainstorming as it does for detailed project planning.

If you are someone who likes clarity and organization when working or studying, Notion is an incredibly powerful tool. Once you get used to it, it becomes hard to imagine managing information any other way.

text_raw:
Gen AI is BAD, FORCED PAYMENT. So basically the constant advances and pushing of AI from the app itself has been increasing constantly to the point where, you’ll accidentally click on the AI stuff and it tries to force you to use it. 


This is only ONE of the negatives, but the worst part is once you run out of free storage you are FORCED to purchase more storage or you have to just make a new account altogether. This is because even if you delete things to make more space it doesn’t actually give you your storage back meaning, you deleted it for nothing because you still don’t have any space. Once you run out of space it prevents you from actually being able to even add bullet points or any feature outside of typing and even that is limited. You can’t add anything at all once you run out of storage, deleting things doesn’t give you more storage, and you literally have 0 other options. This is horrible, like genuinely everyone should find better alternatives because this is just ridiculous, personally I WILL be finding alternatives and stop using notion.

text_raw:
Don't Be Like Me. I've been a moderate-heavy user for over a year and I would never pay for this software. 

No matter where you use it, tables are an atrocious disappointment and the general UI is cumbersome at best. On mobile, where I need it the most, it seemingly can barely handle 50 short lines of plain text without crashing.

Maybe it's great the way other people use it, or maybe the people who sing its praises just don't know what non-Apple software is like and overvalue surface aesthetics.

Either way, unless you only take notes on Mac and you don't have much to actually write down, give this one a pass. I'm only still here trying to finesse it to do the bare minimum of what I need because of switching costs.

text_raw:
AI might be good for some, but for me it was the end. Years ago, I was recommended this note tool via word of mouth. I initially loved it! Being able to switch between devices as I needed was a big plus for my writing, and I loved the stacking folders and clean ui. 

I had no need for ai when it launched. It was unobtrusive, however, so I carried on. Then, a badly implemented update caused a piece of writing I had worked on for hours to, with an easy keyboard stumble, be completely rewritten. Completely. Hours of work chewed up and spit out into slush. :/ I promptly closed the app and stopped writing in it.  

Years later, I have found a software I like better, with no intrusive ai and no cloud services, so my notes are no longer at risk in a server I don't have access to. I have zero faith that notion has kept anything I ever wrote secure. They continue to say one thing and do another. I am done. 

In logging in to transfer my notes, I notice that the program is buggy and slow in ways it never was years ago. Buffers like crazy. It's actually kind of heartbreaking to see how far this app has fallen.

There are better options out there, with more security and better customization. Even if you want ai in a notes app, there are more clean and helpful options that do not compromise your experience. Why pick notion? I never will again.

text_raw:
Each update fixes some breaks others. The latest update left my iPhone 12 Pro Max unable to let me to change the cover image. The change cover page crashes just as the change cover page appears.

Previous review:
Just noticed that I, a paying Notion Plus subscriber can no longer use Notion AI.  Welp, I’m definitely not going to use Notion AI now that I have to upgrade and pay more than 4 times what I normally pay yearly.  And you can’t turn it off or even hide it!  Everyone knows AI is very flawed and yet these tech companies want to charge so much for it!  And anyone who uses Notion knows how flawed it is, which makes it all the more frustrating.  It’s got a truly great structure to it making it incredibly versatile, but it’s like a plane with small wings and no engines.  But hey, you can pay for a somewhat dim flight attendant.

OK, this is my previous review:

Just updated the app, sad to see image files load but then turn white and require me to scroll back up and then over the images to get them to show. Every time I load the page with images in it I have to scroll up and down again. The white screen may not seem like much but it’s annoying in dim light or when updating a journal in bed at night with the lights out. Been using Notion for 8 months now and am kind of surprised this hasn’t been fixed yet.

My original review: it really needs a few things—most importantly, encryption for us poor folks. It looks like you have to be an enterprise customer to get anything resembling actual privacy and it’s unclear what you get is encryption. We live in a time where our data is making people tons of money. I’d rather they not make money off of my notes and my used habits. Also, this needs the same notes graph/map/diagram thingy that a few Notion competitors have that allows you to visualize how all of your notes are related to each other. It is such a cool and helpful way to see the big picture on your projects! The third thing I think it needs is just a slightly better UI. It does a lot but it can be pretty challenging to navigate/find everything. I haven’t checked yet but I suspect that YouTube is the user’s friend along these lines. Otherwise, Notion is a fricken Swiss Army Knife app—you can literally keep a journal, a journal within a journal, a wiki, multiple wikis, I can’t even list all the templates this thing has. It’s really nuts how much you can do with Notion! I just wish it had encryption and the other couple things it’s competition has.

text_raw: Wish it didn’t have AI. Had to delete because of the AI. Obviously AI is not only terrible for the environment (uses so much water without recycling it) and contributes to cognitive decline (our brains need to stretch and work doing even “simple” things to build and maintain key neural pathways), it’s also a massive security risk AND the generative aspect of it straight up just doesn’t work, like you end up typing like four or five prompts in and faffing about refining the result that it would have taken less time just to write whatever you were trying to make the AI write. As much as I hate AI, I really really loved Notion and I would have kept it if they’d have some option for toggling off the AI features. They’re just really obtrusive and obnoxious for how useless/harmful they are, like I don’t want an AI assistant helping me write and stealing my content. But rather than remove or add an off-switch, the developers just kept cramming more AI slop in there, so I’ve had to delete it. It’s such a crying shame. I recalled loved Notion. I’d come back in a heartbeat if they ditched the AI slop.

Thank you!

Just a suggestion from us more simple folk.  Ha!   

Oh and a quick note/todo add widget would be nice. 

Thank you for your time.

text_raw:
Finally found a system that works with my brain. I’ve tried a lot of productivity and organization apps over the years, but Notion is the first one that actually feels flexible enough to grow with how I think instead of forcing me into someone else’s system.

I originally started using it for notes and organization, but it quickly became a place where I could connect ideas, workflows, AI concepts, healthcare operations, and long-term planning in a way that feels natural and visual.

What I appreciate most is that it works for both structured thinking and creative thinking at the same time. I can build detailed workflow maps one minute and brainstorm future ideas the next without switching platforms.

As someone working in healthcare operations and AI workflow design, I also love how adaptable it is for building living systems instead of static documents.

It genuinely helped me feel more organized, focused, and excited about my ideas again.

text_raw: The iPad App is basically view-only. I will start by saying I love Notion. I use it to organize both my work and personal lives. The Notion app on iPad lacks so many features (calendar, etc) or glitches (moves the screen down when trying to type, so you cannot see the text as you type it) as to make it almost impossible to edit or create pages on an iPad. Extremely disappointing given how much success I have had using Notion in my professional life - I was hoping to replicate that in my personal life, but that would involve the iPad app working…

 Structured Context: The ability to seamlessly organize markdown files (⁠.md⁠), system configurations, and project documentation makes it incredibly easy to pull structured data into an AI context.
 Clean Markdown Support: Because Notion handles markdown natively, exporting clean, structured data for programmatic use or CLI tools is seamless.
 Frictionless Organization: It provides a highly scannable, deeply organized hierarchy that keeps massive amounts of technical data manageable without feeling overwhelming.
Whether you are mapping out logic or building a dynamic knowledge base for AI agents to query, Notion bridges the gap between human planning and machine execution perfectly. Highly recommended for anyone running modern, agentic workflows.

Honestly, it’s just too much for me. I’ll stick to journaling on paper—it’s simpler, faster, and actually works.

text_raw: Loving it! BUT I need more colors! So far, after only a day of use, I am absolutely loving Notion. I don’t like when different things are the same color simply because I ran out of options because it ends up getting confusing and ruins the point of the color coding! text_raw:
Notion is NOT okay (updated review). The app is incredibly buggy. Transitioning from my laptop to my phone is such a painful experience. The Notion app is riddled with glitches and bugs. For example, when I create a database and add multi-select options, trying to hold down on one of the options to move it (I sometimes switch the options to be in a certain order) causes the page to spazz out of control and start auto-scrolling back to the top and it doesn’t stop unless I tap out of the page and reenter. This wasn’t an issue before, I could move multi-select options whenever, so why is it happening now? I can’t help but feel like the effort put into maintaining the user experience in the desktop version, whilst adding in new features, isn’t being applied to the app version, which is very disappointing. Creating a great platform for team communication and personal organization, only to have the app’s experience be so glitchy and frustrating, is disheartening. I love Notion and what it has helped me accomplish, but please, take better care of the app. It’s a shame to see so many bugs crawling around such a nice app. 😞
UPDATE 8/13/26: I genuinely cannot stand this app anymore. Forget the Ai updates, can you please just make the app usable?! Please?? This is such a horrible experience on both iPhone AND iPad

text_raw:
Good app, extremely laggy on iPhone. Been using Notion for years, I love the app, and though it takes some time to understand how it all works once you do it’s simple and fun to utilize. 

With that said the app is really really laggy on iPhone. 

A few issues I’ve found using Notion on iPhone:  

1. I cannot delete text on the app. Say I select text and press the x button to delete it on my iPhone keyboard, it will not delete. Even if I press x to delete it without selecting the text it won’t delete so I have to select and press the ‘cut’ selection.

2. Certain pages won’t load when I try to open them, it’ll display the loading icon for awhile and then seemingly crash and close the app.

3. Inserting photos and the page auto-scrolls downwards to the end of the page. Pretty self explanatory, but when I insert photos and then try to move them around the page it’ll start auto scrolling to the bottom of the page. 

4. The app freezing. Sometimes it just freezes and I have to close the app and reopen it. 

5. Accidentally selecting an item (like a divider) and the app won’t let me close the menu that pops up after where the ‘insert below’ option shows up. 


These are just a few issues I’ve found while using the app on iPhone. I truly do love the app, I just don’t like that these issues are so frequent. 

(side note: i have deleted and reinstalled the app in the hopes of fixing these glitches, but it doesn’t fix them.)

text_raw:
Editors, please respond. I love Notion. It's a great app, and I think everyone should have it, it's really good.

I do have a problem with it, though: I can't do as much on mobile as I can on desktop. I know desktop is inherently more powerful, but Notion is just so limiting on mobile. I would love it if you could improve the quality of the mobile version. For example, with a simple table, I cannot add a cell, row, or column on mobile; I have to do that on desktop.

That's only one example. There are so many things entirely possible that I'd love for mobile to do, but it just can't.

I love the app and I'm going to give it 5 stars, but I use mobile 90% of the time and desktop only about 10% of the time. I would really love it if mobile were a lot more powerful.

Thank you.

text_raw: Pretty great until it isn’t. Generally enjoy notion a lot - it’s one of the better note apps out there. The range of features is really good. But - two major problems prevent it from being awesome - you can’t upgrade your subscription! I signed up through Apple and now I want to bring on two other people to my “business” subscription. You can’t do it!!! I have to wait for my current subscription to expire, a month away, or start a new account and. Transfer everything which loses history and maybe some associations. Not much of a business subscription if you can’t more people!!!! The other really really bad thing is app startup time. I open my phone for a morning meeting, go to notion to start AI notes and it just sits there… I’m on WiFi, and the app takes so long to load up it misses the first part of the meeting - often the MOST critical part!  These two things take the app from great to something I can’t rely on. And if I can’t rely on it, then I have to have something else that I can rely on. Really unfortunate. Could be the perfect app - and then isn’t.
